author: reek
body: Everything is polled and fuel-bounded, like every driver on this boot path: completions are recognized by their phase tag, a bit the controller flips on each pass around the completion ring, so a stale entry from the previous lap can never be mistaken for an answer. Data travels by PRP: the first pointer may sit anywhere in a page, the second names the next page when a transfer crosses one, and by keeping each command to eight sectors no transfer ever needs the third form, the PRP list. A two-megabyte seed is a few hundred commands, each answered in microseconds.

author: reek
body: Queue positions live in a state block in memory: submission tail, completion head, and the expected phase tag for each of the two queue pairs. The phase expectation starts at one -- a freshly started controller writes its first lap of completions with the tag set -- and flips whenever the head wraps.

author: reek
body: A transfer's second PRP is the next page boundary when the run crosses one, and zero when it does not; at eight sectors per command no run can touch a third page.

author: reek
body: Ring the submission doorbell with the new tail, then poll the completion queue until the entry at the head carries the expected phase tag. The status field of dword three answers the command; zero is success. Consuming the entry advances the head, flips the phase on wrap, and acknowledges through the completion doorbell.

author: reek
body: CNS 1 identifies the CONTROLLER rather than a namespace; the model number is plain ASCII at bytes 24 through 63 of the returned page. Returns the page address, or zero when the command fails.

author: reek
body: The bring-up resets the controller and creates queues, far too heavy to repeat per read the way the stateless AHCI dispatch does, so the first successful connect publishes its handle to fixed cells and every later call rebuilds the record from them -- the same pattern as the USB disk, magic written LAST so firmware residue cannot impersonate a handle.

author: reek
body: A write ends with an NVM flush: the controller may hold a volatile write cache, and the identity a ceremony just saved must survive the power button -- the same discipline as the IDE path's FLUSH CACHE.

author: reek
body: The single-sector read hands back a fresh buffer, or zero: the shape disk-read-sector's dispatch wants.

author: val
body: Post-ExitBootServices NVMe (PCI class 0x01 subclass 0x08). Modern laptops ship their only internal disk on NVMe: no AHCI port, no legacy IDE, so before this chapter the machine's own storage was simply invisible to the boot payload. The controller is a pair of DMA rings per queue -- submission entries of sixty-four bytes going down, completion entries of sixteen coming back -- and one admin queue pair bootstraps everything else: identify the namespace, create one I/O queue pair, then read and write are two opcodes on the I/O queue.

author: val
body: The registers live behind a 64-bit BAR that real firmware may park above four gigabytes, beyond the boot identity map -- the same lesson the xHCI driver learned -- so the BAR is relocated into the 32-bit MMIO hole post-EBS and the hole's page mapping is installed by the same helper.

author: val
body: CC enables the controller with the NVM command set, four-kilobyte pages, and the entry sizes the spec fixes: submission entries are two-to-the-sixth bytes, completions two-to-the-fourth.

author: val
body: A submission entry is sixteen little-endian dwords. Dword zero carries the opcode and the command identifier; the tail index the entry occupies serves as the identifier, unique among the one command this driver ever has in flight. Dwords six through nine are the two PRP pointers; heap addresses fit in the low dword and the high dwords stay zero.

author: val
body: The namespace's block size hides two indirections deep: FLBAS in the identify data names which LBA format is active, and that format's descriptor carries the size as a power of two. Anything but 512 refuses the disk honestly -- the FAT stack above assumes 512-byte sectors and reading at the wrong granularity is silent corruption, not a smaller disk.

author: val
body: Disable, program the admin queues, enable, then let the admin pair bootstrap the rest. The admin queue addresses must land while the controller is disabled; the spec is explicit that they are latched at enable.

author: val
body: The reachability judgment reads BOTH BAR dwords -- the xHCI driver learned that a packed 64-bit window parks a second device at an address whose low dword looks plausible on its own.
